clue.text: Bird in front of queue is appetising

definitions.note: an adjective cluing a noun: a cocktail is taken before a meal to whet the appetite

indicators.note: one piece placed before another sets the order in which the two parts are joined

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a queue is an old word for a pigtail, a tail of hair

explanation.surface: A bird standing at the head of a line looks tasty to someone hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queue' here is the plaited pigtail, not a line of people. The definition is loose: an aperitif-style drink is the appetising thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail is a drink served before dinner, an appetiser, so the setter defines it by its purpose of stimulating hunger.

clue.text: Little beast with English lump

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the two parts are simply joined

parts.note: a cub is a young animal
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A small animal with an English swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube is a lump, as of sugar or ice: a small solid block.

clue.text: Cheer leader with bird on chimney

definitions.note: describes the answer by its location rather than naming it

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of cheer
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A cheerleader joined by a bird perched on a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheer leader' looks like the pom-pom role; split, it is the leading letter of cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is the hood-shaped cap fitted on top of a chimney stack to improve the draught.

clue.text: I want a new island

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wishing for a new island of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is a large island off the south-east coast of China.

clue.text: Illness in princess's place

parts.note: taken as written
Di was Diana, Princess of Wales, so princess's is Di's
a position is a place

explanation.surface: Sickness in the royal quarters, with the princess unwell at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'in Di's position': Diana, Princess of Wales, was very much in the news in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: An indisposition is a slight illness, the polite word for being unwell.

clue.text: Webbed creature?

parts.note: surface reading: an animal with webbed feet, such as a duck or frog
setter's reading: a creature that spins and lives in a web

explanation.walkthrough: 'Webbed' suggests webbed feet; the question mark warns the web is the silk kind instead.
explanation.definitionFit: This eight-legged arachnid builds a silk web, so it is quite literally a creature of the web.

clue.text: Breathe out twice on 15

definitions.note: describes the answer as something running on rails

parts.note: to puff is to blow out breath
the same piece again

explanation.surface: Someone panting twice over, perched on a fence rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is RAIL, so 'on 15' means running on rails. Puff-puff is British nursery talk for a steam train.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff-puff is a child's word for a steam locomotive, named for its chuffing, and trains run on rails.

clue.text: Gray (Wilde): fashion in early music

parts.note: Dorian Gray is the hero of Oscar Wilde's novel
mode means fashion, as in à la mode

explanation.surface: A literary note on Wilde's Gray and how he dressed in a period of old music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorian mode is one of the medieval church scales, so it belongs to music of the early period.

clue.text: What do you expect with decayed ammunition?

definitions.text: What do you expect with decayed ammunition?

parts.note: surface reading: an exasperated shrug, as if the result were obvious
setter's reading: the result of firing ammunition that has gone bad is a poor, feeble discharge

explanation.walkthrough: The decayed ammunition gives the answer's first word literally, while the whole phrase also means a bad attempt at hitting a target.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotten shot is a poor attempt at hitting a target, just the result decayed rounds would give.

clue.text: Dog entertains in Deutschland — Georgian feature?

indicators.note: a host who entertains has guests inside the house, so one piece holds another

parts.note: bow-wow is a child's word for a dog
taken as written
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A German dog plays host, alongside a puzzle about Georgian architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog swallows the two short pieces in its middle. Georgian here is the 18th-century British architectural period, not the country, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow window is a curved bay window, a typical ornament of Georgian-era houses in Britain.

clue.text: Churchill's hope, hot possibility to bear

parts.note: surface reading: Winston Churchill's wartime hopes
setter's reading: Churchill was nicknamed Winnie, which opens the answer
unexplained: these words fit no clear wordplay and may be garbled in the scanned text

explanation.walkthrough: Only the Churchill link and the definition are clear; the middle of this clue, 'hope, hot possibility to', is not explained, and may be an OCR fault in the scanned text.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is A. A. Milne's honey-loving teddy bear, the best-known bear in children's books.

clue.text: Trees with treetop of gold?

parts.note: firs are conifer trees
the top of tree is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Trees topped with gilded tips, like a Christmas decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treetop' must be split: tree, then its top. Gold stands for first place, as in a gold medal, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold medal is awarded for winning, so gold is a stand-in for coming top in a competition.

clue.text: Exceedingly archaic piano string on single-track road

parts.note: passing is an archaic word for exceedingly, as in passing fair
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a lace is a string for tying a shoe

explanation.surface: Something exceedingly old, a piano string, found on a lonely country road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceedingly archaic' reads as one description, but 'archaic' only labels PASSING as an old sense of 'exceedingly'. Single-track roads, common in rural Britain, have wider spots where cars can pull over.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing place is a widened lay-by on a narrow road where vehicles can pull in to let oncoming traffic go by.

clue.text: Contrived air-lift: CIA fixed it

indicators.note: the CIA has rigged the material, so the letters are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A staged airlift operation: the American spy agency rigged it.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan reads 'air-left', but the letters need 'air-lift', a supply operation by aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Artificial means contrived or forced, not natural or genuine.

clue.text: Scattered and lost, owing to 18?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dispersed and squandered, as energy or a fortune

definitions.note: describes someone made dissolute by heavy drinking
definitions.meaning: second meaning: debauched as a result of 18, the drunkenness answer

explanation.walkthrough: 18 points to the drunkenness answer; someone ruined by it is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissipated means both wasted or dispersed and dissolute, given over to drinking and pleasure.

clue.text: Bird on (or opposed to) road

definitions.note: rail against means to be opposed to
definitions.meaning: second meaning: placed before road it makes railroad, and to complain against something is to do this

explanation.walkthrough: The clue loosely packs three hints: a bird, a word that goes in front of road, and one that means protest against.
explanation.definitionFit: The rail is a family of wading birds; the verb rail means to protest bitterly, and with road it forms railroad.

clue.text: Unpleasantness arising from Mexico/US involvement with the Financial Times

indicators.note: things that become involved get tangled up together, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
FT is the usual short name of the Financial Times, a London newspaper

explanation.surface: A diplomatic row between Mexico and America gets a London financial paper involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unpleasantness arising' reads as a political row; here it is something unpleasant that literally rises into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Toxic fumes are poisonous gases that rise from a source, an unpleasant thing that goes up into the air.

clue.text: Cancel entry when a relative is on top

indicators.note: in a down light the piece on top comes first, ahead of the other

parts.note: taken as written
bro is short for brother
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Annul someone's admission whenever a family member outranks them.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate is to repeal or abolish a law or agreement formally.

clue.text: Fashionable drunkard eating cheese at start of year's drunkenness

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of year

explanation.surface: A trendy drinker tucks into cheese at a New Year binge.
explanation.walkthrough: Brie is a soft French cheese; the cheese goes inside the drunkard, and the whole sits between the fashionable word and the year's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Insobriety is the formal noun for the state of being drunk, the opposite of sobriety.

clue.text: Old expression of surprise in periods of boredom

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, straddling two of them

parts.note: the letters span the end of periods and the start of of

explanation.surface: Someone in olden days exclaiming during long dull stretches of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Odso is an obsolete mild oath, a softened form of 'God's so', used to express surprise.

clue.text: Weighing machine for fish?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an apparatus for weighing

definitions.note: what fish have, not a synonym
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the small bony plates covering a fish

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a fishmonger's weighing machine; the question mark flags the fish's own covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Scales are the weighing device and also the hard overlapping plates on a fish's skin.

clue.text: God announces himself in disregard of the consequences

parts.note: introducing oneself starts 'I'm ...'
Providence is God seen as the power guiding events

explanation.surface: A deity proclaims who he is, heedless of what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The deity's self-introduction is 'I'm Providence', run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvidence is failing to provide for the future, a lack of foresight about what will follow from one's actions.

clue.text: Opposed to a drink

parts.note: taken as written
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone who disapproves of having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is dialect for against, so it means opposed to.

clue.text: Obstetrician's direction to printer

indicators.note: the possessive says the answer belongs to the word, held within its letters

parts.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: A doctor who delivers babies gives instructions to a printer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is Latin for 'let it stand', the proof-reader's instruction to ignore a marked correction.

clue.text: Train smash within

indicators.note: a smash breaks something into pieces that land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A railway crash happens inside something.
explanation.definitionFit: Intra is the Latin prefix meaning inside, as in intravenous and intramural.

clue.text: One thing left may be wanted for advertising

parts.words: One thing left may be wanted for advertising
parts.note: surface reading: the last remaining item might be put up for sale in an advert
setter's reading: a glowing tube of the kind used in shop signs

explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'One thing left' is not fully explained here; the answer rests on the definition and every crossing letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing gas-filled tubes have long been the standard material of illuminated shop and billboard signs.

clue.text: Student, arithmetician, on the way up?

definitions.note: a cryptic hint at something you climb, not a synonym

parts.note: L is a learner, from the learner-driver plate
an adder is one who adds, a joke name for anyone doing sums

explanation.surface: A pupil good at maths is climbing the career ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver shows an L plate, so L stands for any learner or student.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder is what someone stands on while climbing upward, so it is the thing you are on when going up.

clue.text: Head after thorax? It's the old story

indicators.note: one part following another fixes their order: the second named comes first

parts.note: the thorax is the chest
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: An anatomy lesson: what comes after the thorax, apparently an old tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is an old, much-repeated joke or tale, one heard too many times.
